name: look
description: Look through the camera and answer a question about what is in view (objects, text, people, colors, counts). Use whenever the user asks what you see, what they are holding, or anything about the physical scene.

question.description: The user's question about the scene, e.g. 'what brand is this' or 'how many people are here'. Leave empty for a general description.

name: take_photo
description: Save a photo of the current camera view (including zoom) to the session folder.

label.description: Optional short label for the file name, e.g. 'front bumper'.

name: start_recording
description: Start recording video of the camera view.

max_seconds.description: Optional. Stop automatically after this many seconds.

name: stop_recording
description: Stop the current video recording and save it.

name: zoom
description: Zoom the camera view. Use target to zoom onto a specific object, direction for 'zoom in' or 'zoom out', or level for an exact amount (1 = full wide view, up to 8).

target.description: Object to zoom onto, e.g. 'the label on the bottle'.

name: pan
description: Move the zoomed view left, right, up, down, or back to center.

direction.description: left, right, up, down, or center.

name: set_window
description: Change the camera window: fullscreen, windowed, wide, tall, small, large, fit (show whole image), fill (fill window, crop edges), pin (always on top), unpin, or custom with width and height.

mode.description: fullscreen, windowed, wide, tall, small, large, fit, fill, pin, unpin, or custom.

width.description: Window width in pixels, only for custom.

height.description: Window height in pixels, only for custom.

name: read_text
description: Read all text visible to the camera (documents, labels, whiteboards). By default copies it to the clipboard.

then.description: copy (default, puts it on the clipboard), save (adds it to notes), or say (just read it back).

name: look_at_screen
description: Take a screenshot of the user's computer screen and answer a question about it.

question.description: What the user wants to know about their screen.

name: save_note
description: Write something down in the session notes.

name: search_web
description: Open a web search in the user's browser. Useful after look, e.g. to find where to buy or learn about an object.

name: open_item
description: Open something on the computer: the captures folder, the last photo, the last video, the notes, or the report.

what.description: folder, last_photo, last_video, notes, or report.

name: make_report
description: Build a report of this session (photos with AI captions, videos, notes, observations) plus a written summary, then open it.

purpose.description: What the report is for, e.g. 'insurance claim', 'home inventory', 'lab notes'. Shapes the summary.

name: watch_for
description: Keep watching the camera in the background and alert when something appears (e.g. 'a person', 'my dog', 'the package'). Takes a photo when it happens. Pass target 'stop' to stop watching.

name: follow_me
description: Turn auto-framing on or off. When on, the view automatically zooms and pans to keep the user's face centered, like a camera operator.

on.description: true to start following, false to stop.

name: sleep
description: Stop listening. Use when the user says be quiet, go to sleep, stop listening, mute, or that's all. The user presses Space to wake you.

name: set_autonomy
description: Change how independent you are. off: only act when asked. aware: quietly track what's happening but only speak when spoken to. proactive: speak up on your own when something notable happens (someone arrives, holds something up, a new person joins).

name: turn_camera
description: Physically turn the robot's camera head left or right (it's a pan-only servo, no up/down). It normally follows the user's face on its own; use this when asked to look left, look right, or back to center.

degrees.description: Optional. How far to turn, default 25.

name: track_object
description: Lock onto any object in view (a mug, a phone, a pet) and keep it in view: the servo head and zoom follow it instead of the user's face. Pass target 'stop' to go back to following faces.

target.description: What to track, e.g. 'the red mug', or 'stop'.
